relevance_note: One index case is described individually with a homozygous ABCA1 variant and Tangier disease: "one IC with a variant in ABCA1 in homozygosity causing Tangier disease".
method_note: Hand extraction, no table transcription script. Paper is a 7-index-case series of low HDL/LDL dyslipidaemias; only Index case 1 (ABCA1, Tangier) is in scope; index cases 2-7 (LCAT, APOB, unsolved) get no rows and are counted in cohort_size_as_stated = 7. Label 'Index case 1' chosen from the section heading/figure legend (the paper also uses 'IC1', 'Patient 1' and Table 1 ID '1'). Relatives of Index case 1 (parents of a consanguineous couple, a 'healthy younger brother', 'two healthy sons') were neither tested nor described as affected ('No relatives were available for cascade screening'; sons/parents only called 'obligatory' carriers), so they were not given rows under the tested-or-affected scope rule. Inheritance left 'not reported' because the parents' carrier status is an authors' inference, not testing. Age: Table 1 gives Age 42 while the text says she was 48 years old at referral (first MI and lab tests at 42); last evaluation recorded as 48 years-old from the text; onset left not reported (first MI at 42 but tonsillectomy at 4 years of unstated cause). Transcript NM_005502 is mapped to ABCA1 only via the Methods 'respectively' list (printed as 'NM_ NM_005502'). Lipid values without an explicit 'low/high' qualifier (ApoA1 10 mg/dl, TC 73, TG 158) were not turned into features or checklist statuses; low LDL is recorded because the text says 'LDL levels were already low'. 'Normal ophthalmological and neurological exam' is a whole-examination statement: recorded as excluded 'abnormal ophthalmological exam' / 'abnormal neurological exam' only; corneal opacity and peripheral neuropathy checklist items left not reported (D-27). No stacked cells. No internal contradictions beyond the Table 1 age versus text age.
